key_insight: inClinico Agent combines machine-learning trial-success predictions with LLM tools, forecasting primary endpoint outcomes across phases I–IV rather than discovering cancer drugs.
clinical_relevance: The system could inform trial planning and research prioritization, but the abstract does not establish cancer-specific performance or patient benefit.
method: Train separate models for efficacy and safety/toxicity primary endpoints.
Use registration-time trial features and frozen literature embeddings to limit outcome leakage.
Combine probability scores with LLMs, retrieval tools and specialized clinical skills.
evidence_signal: For trials initiated in 2021 or later, AUROC was 0.828 for efficacy (n=2,347) and 0.809 for safety/toxicity (n=1,485); ClinicoBench adds prospective tracking of 3,235 ongoing trials.
watch_item: Prospective predictive accuracy remains to be established as benchmark trials complete.
paper_title: inClinico Agent for clinical trial endpoint prediction and prospective evaluation
